title: Traffic warmup & spike containment playbook — May 2026 (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This playbook describes an operational procedure for controlled traffic warmup and containment of unexpected spikes during a release window. Aim: keep tail latency under SLOs, avoid cascading OOM/queue drops, and give clear operator steps for fast mitigation.

Audience:
- Release engineers on-call
- SRE/Platform owners
- Release conductor (product/pm on watch)

Overview
1) Warmup phase (T-minus 72h → T-minus 0):
   - T-72h: staging e2e traffic ramp to 20% production profile. Run smoke suite (smoke-suite/v2).
   - T-48h: run canary cohort (5% prod) for 6 hours, collect tail p99.9 & kv-cache hit rate.
   - T-24h: increase to 25–40% traffic with burst tests (10x short bursts) to validate autoscale.
   - T-4h: run full smoke + load-replay (replay-id: replay/2026-05-04/alpha). Verify model-routing heuristics.

Warmup checklist (operators):
- [ ] Confirm model pinned versions in routing config (route: /text/generate)
- [ ] Validate batcher config and max-batch-latency knobs in staging
- [ ] Ensure cache priming job completed (job: cache-prime-2026-05-02)
- [ ] Nightly telemetry check: token-cost delta < 12% vs baseline

2) Rollout calendar (compact view)
   - Day -3 (May 1): staging smoke + cache prime
   - Day -2 (May 2): canary 5% start 09:00; check at 15:00
   - Day -1 (May 3): canary expand 20% 10:00–16:00; run burst tests 14:00
   - Day 0 (May 4): soft launch 50% at 11:00; monitor 11:00–13:00, then 100% at 14:00 if green

Monitoring signals (immediate abort thresholds):
- p99 latency increases > 40% sustained for 10m → abort and rollback to prior model version
- Queue depth > 300 for more than 2m on serving pods → immediate throttle + fallback routing
- OOM event > 2 nodes in 5m window → rollback to smaller instance type or revert quantization change

Spike containment quick actions (if thresholds crossed):
1) Engage traffic-gate (route throttles to 10%) via console quick-toggle (ops/traffic-gates)
2) Switch to fallback model-variant: route -> model: rwd-small-quant-v2 (config id: route-fallback-2026-05-04)
3) Disable caching writes (set CACHE_WRITE=off) and clear largest KV shards sequentially (shard ids listed in /ops/cache/shards-to-evict)
4) Scale up queue processors by +30% (autoscaler override) for 10 minutes and watch queue metrics
5) Post-mortem kick: open incident INF-2043 and add immediate notes (who, when, action taken)

Smoke test snippet (commands):
- run smoke-suite --profile=prod-sample --duration=10m --report=artifacts/smoke-2026-05-04.json
- gh pr checkout 471 && ./tools/run-local-bench --replay replay/2026-05-04/alpha

Release notes (draft - to be polished for customer-facing brief):
- Feature: model-serving kernel selection improved for long context workloads (reduced p99 by ~12% in bench)
- Operational: new traffic-gate quick-toggle and fallback routing for faster containment
- Known issues: under heavy short-burst traffic some autoscaler configs can overreact; mitigation: tuned throttle curve (rolling)

Communication templates
- Slack (ops-alerts): "Launching soft-start for /text/generate at 11:00 UTC. Watch p99/p50/queue-depth. Use #release-ops for comms. If p99 > 40% abort."
- Pager (on-call): "ONCALL: traffic warmup in progress. Abort thresholds set. Refer runbook: confluence/redwood/RE/TrafficWarmup"

Roles & responsibilities (day-of)
- Release conductor: Aisha Patel — overall go/no-go
- SRE lead: Jonah Kim — telemetry and canary validation
- Serving runtime lead: Maya Lopez — rollback, model-variant toggles
- Support liaison: Ethan Wright — customer comms and release notes update

Post-release checklist (T+0 to T+72h):
- [ ] 24h retrospective notes in this doc (section: postmortem notes)
- [ ] Telemetry export and compare (baseline vs post) for token-cost, p95, p99
- [ ] Run quality checks on sampled outputs; flag regressions to model-quality@redwood.ai

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can we add an automated rollback when queue-depth X AND p99 Y cross together? (Jonah to prototype)
- Validate that cache-evict script is safe on Dedicated nodes (Maya to run a dry-run)

Appendix: quick links and snippets
- Ops toggle console: https://console.redwood.ai/ops/traffic-gates
- Incident template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/Release+Incident+Template
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/471

Notes to self: rough cut — compress for external release notes, leave technical appendix for SRE playbook. Keep this doc as the single source-of-truth during the May 4 rollout.
